title: Set newState stale after rollback/post-commit fail
description:
/set reports newState == oldState after backend writes in rollback and post-commit failure paths (RFC 8620 §5.3: newState is "The state string that will now be returned by Foo/get"). Batch 8b review (JMAP-y3f2.19, JMAP-8mem.3).

1. crate-jmap-chat-server/src/chat.rs ~L887-950: the direct-chat recheck rollback (create_object L887, destroy_object L913/L943) and the lost-race / cleanup-failed branches never set `mutated` (only L994/1263/1271/1358 do). If it is the only change in the batch, finalize_set_response (L1386) returns newState == oldState though backend Chat state moved; if destroy also fails (Err arm ~L917) the Chat stays live while newState is stale, so a client never sees it via /changes from that state.
2. crate-jmap-chat-server/tests/integration.rs:2607 chat_set_direct_recheck_read_failure_rolls_back_create arms only queue_chat_get_fault_after_create(). Add the read-fail + destroy-fail case (queue_chat_get_fault_after_create() plus inject("Chat","destroy")): assert notCreated is a redacted serverFail, no canary leaks, and newState != oldState.
3. crate-jmap-vtc-server/src/participant.rs:374-382: VTCParticipant create stores the participant (create_object L374) then runs `set_call_state(...).await?` (L381). A backend error there reports the stored join as notCreated with `mutated` false, so newState can equal oldState. Treat it like run_effects: best-effort after commit, and count the commit as a mutation. (Stale-snapshot overwrite is tracked on JMAP-ace5.)
close_reason: Batch 9: committed and adversarially verified; CI green at df7e2035
